excerpt: You are almost entirely forest, and you hold more fresh water per person than almost any nation in Africa.
paras: You are almost entirely forest, and you hold more fresh water per person than almost any nation in Africa. Yet you borrow at more than nine percent. The forest that cools the planet should lower the price of your capital, not sit outside your balance sheet.

Your partners are building beside you. In February 2026 the World Bank approved $150 million for piped water, electricity and sanitation, after $150 million in 2025 for your cities. In 2023 you converted $500 million of your debt into a lasting commitment to your ocean. In 2026 you raised 106.5 billion CFA francs on the bond market of Central Africa, at rates well below those you pay abroad.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. At the last count, in 1995, only twenty in every hundred of your young people completed lower secondary school, a figure so old that it must be measured again. Your health services reach 48 on the World Health Organization index, less than half of full coverage. Thirty-nine in every hundred of your city dwellers live in slums. Schooling sets your Coverage today, at 20.2 out of 100, with health and shelter close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Gabon: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Gabonese falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: Your forest cools the planet. Let it lower the price of your debt.
